summary: The draft is a coherent, uniquely identifiable I01-E05 category-level annual growth plan. Recalculated plan, cost, quarterly KPI, workload, and Q3 recovery arithmetic reconcile; the sample/real boundary is strong. Full replacement-register traceability is not yet reliable: 17 entries route target facts to the wrong source key, and 32 entries misclassify counts, rates, or money as period/date values. The requested four-category check is only demonstrated for three sample categories. Real personal-data handling remains a high-level hold condition rather than an operational procedure.

findings.acceptance_impact: Correct before treating the register as a reliable REAL replacement map.
findings.locator: §4 paragraph 2-3 and §12.2 register; draft lines 521-539, fact IDs SF-00185-SF-00196, SF-00199-SF-00201, SF-00203; plus §10 Table 10-2 Q4 new-course row, SF-00588 at draft line 924.
findings.finding: Sixteen §4 facts that are 2027 target values or target-derived calculations are keyed SRC-BASELINE: SF-00185-SF-00196, SF-00199-SF-00201, and SF-00203. The source map defines SRC-BASELINE as comparison-year source material and SRC-TARGET/SRC-GROWTH for annual plan targets and comparisons. Separately, SF-00588 is the synthetic Q4 course ID but points to SRC-EVIDENCE, whose §12.1 sources are the four evidence types; the course ID should resolve to an authorized course schedule/target source such as SRC-QUARTER or SRC-TARGET. The displayed numbers and locators are readable, but the wrong keys can send a REAL replacement to the wrong source class.
findings.resolution: Remap each §4 row to the source key appropriate to its 2027 target or derived comparison, and remap SF-00588 to the real course schedule/plan source; retain the exact row and field locator.

findings.acceptance_impact: Correct the register's fact-type metadata before downstream typed replacement or automated checking.
findings.finding: These 32 entries use fact_type '期間／日期欄值' for non-date values: class/capacity counts and evidence-unit counts, KPI numerators/denominators, and NTD amounts. Examples: SF-00206 labels NTD 9,000 as a date/period; SF-00250 labels NTD 56,310 as a date/period; SF-00304 labels 7 classes as a date/period. The value, locator and source key remain visible, so this does not erase the facts, but the type metadata is not dependable.
findings.resolution: Reclass each listed row according to its field as quantity, ratio/calculated value, or amount; retain valid duration/year entries in the period/date class.

findings.acceptance_impact: Applies only if the requested '4 category' criterion means four distinct categories.
findings.finding: The worked plan compares only A/B/C. It provides usable category-level mechanics, but no fourth example category. The official requirement and Blueprint do not set a four-category count, and no real association category list was supplied; therefore the absence is a limitation against the literal review-scope wording, not evidence that an actual association category was omitted.
findings.resolution: If four sample categories were intended, add a fourth fully linked sample category and recalculate all totals; otherwise confirm the intended scope outside this review. No fourth REAL category is inferred.

findings.acceptance_impact: Do not use the REAL replacement path with identifiable enrolment or feedback data until the applicable policy and handling steps are verified and documented.
findings.locator: §3 Table 3-1 B row line 84; §6 Table 6-2 line 154; §8 Table 8-2 enrolment/feedback rows lines 204-206; §10 Table 10-2 lines 247-250 and Table 10-4 lines 288-292; §12.1 SRC-NEED/SRC-QUARTER/SRC-EVIDENCE lines 318, 325-327; §13 steps 4 and 6 lines 939-941.
findings.finding: The draft correctly labels all worked data synthetic and mentions personal-data/file-management checks, de-identification, and stopping commitments when protection conditions are unclear. It does not define a practical REAL workflow for purpose and permitted fields, notice/authorization as applicable, role-based access, secure storage, retention/deletion, or incident handling, and it does not point to an association policy or competent review. Official privacy texts address purpose/necessity, collection notice, data maintenance/deletion, and security measures; see the bound legal references. This is a readiness gap, not a finding of unlawful collection or a statutory breach.
findings.resolution: Before REAL use, map the association's actual data sources and applicable policy/authority to a minimal-data, access, storage, retention/deletion, de-identification, and incident-response workflow; have the responsible privacy/legal authority verify the effective rules.
